analysis.title: What Matters Today: Jensen is back. NVDA Soars, Memory - Strong 2027, A More Measured 2028, The Causes and Consequences of a Low-Hire, Low-Fire Labor Market
key_insights: NVDA added about $940bn of market cap in one day on Jensen's reinstatement (GIR take). The US desk saw an early chase with the name up more than 30% and macro hedges being taken off.
Desk activity was a 5 out of 10. HFs were busier managing short books (NVDA demand, select tech names, macro expressions) while LOs were quiet. NDX constituent volumes were up about 60%.
After two weeks of relentless supply in NVDA, primarily from long-only holders, supply abatement was a big component of the move magnitude.
NDX rose more than 5% in a single day. Comparable moves (Apr 2025, Nov 2022, Mar 2020, Dec 2018) each came at or near local market lows.

Investor feedback is mostly uncertain. Bulls cite a 'nobody left to sell' positioning tailwind and a sentiment-driven rather than fundamental AI/Semis bear market. Bears cite China, shell/permitting, ROIs and token trajectory, and see difficulty rallying much above pre-Election levels.
GS stays constructive on 2027 memory fundamentals with meaningful DRAM and HBM undersupply, but now expects a smaller industry undersupply in 2028E.

GS revises conventional DRAM pricing to +32%/-19% YoY for 2027E/2028E (from +32%/-5%) and NAND to +20%/-21% (from +30%/-14%). HBM TAM estimates rise to US$60bn/US$200bn/US$237bn for 2026E/2027E/2028E.

Samsung and Hynix share prices are said to price in zero AI capex growth in 2028E and an additional 40% ASP decline versus the base case. GS remains constructive given about 20% shareholder return yields.
LTA default risk: conventional DRAM prices would need to fall more than 32-54% below the GS base case over two years before customers have a meaningful incentive to default on LTAs.

For Kioxia, GS factors in a gradual price decline from Apr-Jun 2027, cutting FY3/28-29 OP estimates by 15%/30% (FY3/27E unchanged). EPS revisions are modest because the share price implies larger buybacks, and the 100% surplus FCF return policy could mean over 30% FY3/28E TSR yield.
GS models CXMT starting HBM revenue next year, limited to HBM2E and HBM3 and a small fraction of the TAM.

Labor market: churn explains most of the recent decline in worker turnover. AI exposure is emerging as a driver, with churn lower in industries with higher AI adoption and young workers' job-prospect perceptions deteriorating.
Depressed churn is estimated to weigh on YoY wage growth by about 0.3pp. GS expects turnover to pick up somewhat, but persistent low turnover could dampen productivity growth.
